notes:
Recent discovery: finance + infra are aligned on business case but need firm SLA and capacity plan. Workshop ask: produce a binding GPU reservation plan showing 95th-pct latency SLOs and worst-case token/sec during product launch.

Key constraints/asks from Silverpine:
- Must support chat front-end (agent assist) + nightly bulk embeddings pipeline.
- Data residency: primary EU data slices for EU customers; VPC peering required.
- KMS/HSM required for customer PII. SOC2 attestation expected.
- Cost sensitivity: total infra TCO must be justified vs cloud burst + managed API.

Preliminary sizing targets (customer-provided traffic):
- Chat (interactive): baseline 300 QPS steady-state across instances, peak up to 1,200 QPS during marketing events. Typical session = 30 tokens/user turn, avg 7 turns.
- Embeddings (search index updates): batch window nightly, target throughput 50k tokens/sec sustained for 45 minutes during index refresh.
- Reranking: low-latency path, p95 < 150ms target for top-10 reranks at 200 QPS.

Model preferences + routing policy:
- Primary model: quantized 70B open-weight chat model (customer wants 8-bit/llm-int8 setup).
- Fallbacks: 13B/30B variants for cost-mode and overflow. Routing: route to cheaper variant for non-critical background jobs; strict route-to-primary for front-line chat.

POC notes: Ran 48-hour POC in Redwood Dedicated trial (4x A100 80GB equivalent): observed ~p95 generation latency 230ms for 70B quantized at 250 QPS; embeddings batch throughput peaked at ~32k tokens/sec (single pool). Customer expects 40-50% higher throughput for production peak — hence workshop to size reserve.

Stated priorities from CTO quote: "We need predictable tail latency and a hard SLA for market-critical windows — can't rely on burst credits alone."

Expectations from Redwood: provide reserved GPU plan (metric-backed), latency SLO proposals (p50/p95/p99 targets by route), cost modeling for reserved vs burst, and an operations playbook for canary rollouts and failover to smaller model variants.
